what_it_does: This paper presents a camera sensor (the kind found in smartphones) built as three stacked layers of silicon, where each layer captures light differently. The sensor is special because it can switch between two operating modes: a high-resolution 'rolling shutter' mode (50 megapixels) that captures light row-by-row but is prone to motion blur and flickering artifacts, and a lower-resolution 'global shutter' mode (12.5 megapixels) that exposes the entire sensor at once, eliminating those artifacts but traditionally producing noisier images. By smartly combining both architectures in a single 3-layer stack, the sensor can flip between modes on demand—giving users the best of both without having to choose between them.
